chunks: And it is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Yazid ibn Khalifah who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Umar ibn Hanzalah brought us from you a time [for prayer].' He said, 'Then he does not lie to us.' I said, 'He said,' 'The time for Maghrib is when the sun's disk disappears, except that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to delay Maghrib if the journey was strenuous, and he would combine it with Isha.' He said, 'He is truthful.'
And he said, 'The time for the later Isha is when the twilight disappears until one-third of the night, and the time for Fajr is when it appears until it brightens.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific times for Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the precise astronomical markers for prayer times, specifically defining Maghrib by the disappearance of the sun's disk and Isha by the fading of twilight (*shafaq*). It highlights the Prophetic precedent (*Sunnah*) of combining prayers during travel, a practice widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence as evidence for *Jam' al-Taqdim* (early combination), while also delineating the window for Fajr from dawn's appearance until full brightness. The chain of transmission through Yunus ibn Abi 'Urwah underscores the reliability of these temporal definitions within the Imami scholarly tradition.
